overall: The AG declined to review the complaints about the Vice Chair's open-session remarks, finding no Open Meeting Law issue, and found the October 23 notice sufficiently specific, so no violation occurred.

allegations.summary: Vice Chair allegedly disparaged the complainant's character in open session at the October 23 meeting, which the complainant said was meant to chill oversight.
allegations.key_passage: Although we certainly discourage uncivil and unprofessional behavior, an allegation of unprofessional conduct or incivility does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that discussion of his character should have been held in executive session under Purpose 1 rather than in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Discussion of a person’s character and discussion of Open Meeting Law Complaints, for example, may be discussed in executive session but need not be.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 23 notice was not specific enough because it did not list the Vice Chair's discussion of his character as a topic.
allegations.key_passage: Based upon our review of all the information before us, we find that even if Vice Chair’s comments did not fall within the discussion topic “Open Meeting Law Complaints – Christopher Kelleher,” they were not reasonably anticipated by the chair.
